battle.title: Binary Search Blitz
battle.description: Halve the range, find the target, beat the clock.

questions.text: What must be true about an array before binary search can be used on it?
options: It must contain no duplicate values
Its length must be a power of two
It must contain only positive numbers
questions.explanation: Binary search discards half the range by comparing with the middle, which is only valid when the data is ordered. Duplicates are fine and length and sign do not matter.

questions.text: Roughly how many comparisons does binary search need, at most, on a sorted array of 1000 elements?
questions.explanation: Each step halves the range, and log2(1000) is just under 10, so about 10 comparisons suffice. 500 or 1000 describes a linear scan.
Probes are index 2 (5 < 7, go right), index 4 (9 > 7, go left) and index 3 (found), so the index is 3 after 3 probes. Guessing 2 steps forgets the first probe that goes right.

questions.text: A sorted array has millions of values, possibly repeated. For many queries you need the FIRST position whose value is >= x. What is best?
options: A linear scan from the start for each query
Copy and sort the array for every query, then scan
Put the values in a HashSet and look up x
Binary search that keeps narrowing to the left half even after a match (lower bound)
questions.answer: Binary search that keeps narrowing to the left half even after a match (lower bound)
questions.explanation: The array is already sorted, so each query is O(log n); continuing left after a match finds the first position. A HashSet cannot answer 'first position >= x', and rescanning or re-sorting wastes time.
lo + hi is 3.5 billion, which exceeds the int maximum and wraps negative before being divided. lo + (hi - lo) / 2 never exceeds hi, which is why it is the safe way to compute mid.

debug.title: The Last Candidate
debug.description: The program reads a sorted array of distinct integers and q queries. For each query it should print the index of the value, or -1 if absent. It sometimes prints -1 for values that are present. Input: n, the sorted array, q, then q queries. Output: one index or -1 per query.
hints: Search for 5 in an array that has only one element, [5]. Is it found?
The search works for many values but fails sometimes. Look at the loop condition.
When lo and hi meet there is still one candidate left. Does the loop test that last candidate?
Use while (lo <= hi) so the final remaining element is also checked.
